title: I'm a solo dev building a medieval fantasy daughter-raising sim — here's a date scene from one of the romance routes
author: LDDreamsmith
selftext:
Hi everyone! I'm a solo developer working on Luminara: The Second Dawn — a medieval fantasy daughter-raising sim with adventure and romance elements. AI tools made this game possible for me. But using AI tools involves a lot of detail control, time, and effort. Here are a few tools I have been using for my game — might be helpful to you as well: OpenArt for consistent character design, Suno for music design, and ElevenLabs for sound effects.

You raise your daughter from childhood to adulthood. Study, adventure, make friends, fall in love — every choice shapes her future across 70+ endings.

The game features 7 romanceable characters so far (each with their own storyline and romance route), turn-based combat, merchant trading, and 70+ endings.



This clip shows a date scene with one of the romanceable characters (Cedric).

The game launches into Steam Early Access on October 30, 2026, and a free demo is available now.



🔔 Steam:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4631440/Luminara\_The\_Second\_Dawn/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4631440/Luminara_The_Second_Dawn/)



Happy to answer any questions about the game — and I'd love to hear what tools other devs here are using!

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Visual Novels are the last thing I would consider an LLM for. The writing they deliver is bad, so the primary method of engagement with the game will be poisoned.

It's nice you can get high definition still images and use the best possible framing / stylistic preference of the model, but it's still going to look bad if you need to use an uncensored model and jailbreaking one of the big 3 to produce VN bedroom scenes will get you banned. 

And you just don't need it for the coding. The basic VN coding languages are all dead easy to use; they're built for accessibility.
